text:
kai: Kicking off canary for release/2026-04-12 - routing 4% to chat+embeds. Change window 11:00-15:00 PT. I'll watch SLOs for 15m. release notes: https://internal.redwood/release/2026-04-12 :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary started - job=canary-2026-04-12-4pct, target=chat+embeds, routing=4% :rocket:

sam: Observability shows 429 spike on /v1/chat at 1729999040, baseline 0.02% -> 1.1% in 3m. p95 slightly up but error type is throttling. Dashboard: https://obs.redwood/dash/chat-rate

sre-oncall: Alert filter: `sum(rate(http_responses_total{route="/v1/chat",code="429",deploy_tag="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/chat",deploy_tag="canary"}[5m])) > 0.005` firing. Any new rate-limiter config in this release?

kai: We added adaptive rate-limiter improvements to reduce tail latency under burst, defaulting to a 200rps token bucket on canary nodes. Could the adaptive logic be mis-evaluating capacity and throttling too early?

sam: Traces show internal limiter returning 429 with reason="pool-overload" and logs indicate burst estimate lower than actual capacity due to a mis-tagged cpu label on canary nodes.

sre-oncall: Plan: pause canary routing to 0%, revert adaptive limiter to legacy config for canary, and run a synthetic replay to validate. If replay passes, resume at 1% and monitor. If 429s persist, rollback. Agreed?

kai: Agree. /deploy pause canary job=canary-2026-04-12-4pct (requested by kai)

deploy-bot: Canary paused. Routing set to 0%. Traces sampling increased. Config diff: reverting adaptive-limiter -> legacy-token-bucket (config-change-1729999050).

ash: Starting synthetic replay at 5 rps for 90s against canary pool. Logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/canary-2026-04-12/1729999060

sam: Replay shows 429s gone, p95 normal ~320ms, errors ~0.01%. Good signal.

sre-oncall: Resume to 1% for 10m. If 429 rate stays <0.1% and p95 <500ms continue ramp; else rollback. Rollback command: `deploy-bot rollback canary-2026-04-12 --full`

kai: Resuming to 1% now. /deploy resume canary job=canary-2026-04-12-4pct target=1% (requested by kai)

deploy-bot: Canary ramped to 1%. Observability: high sampling, alert window=5m.

tara: Adding release note: "Mitigation: reverted adaptive rate-limiter on canary due to premature throttling triggered by mislabeled cpu tag; added infra-tagging check to preflight."

kai: Thanks team. Marking REL-2026-04-12 as PAUSED->REVERTED->RESUMED(1%). Will follow up in postmortem with tagging test and limiter regression. :thumbsup:
